articles.title: Manchester City agree £34m deal for Allan Elias as Nico González nears Newcastle move
articles.summary: Palmeiras winger’s arrival paves way for Savinho exit. City monitoring Liverpool forward Cody Gakpo. Manchester City have agreed a €37.5m plus €2.5m (£34m) deal for the Palmeiras winger Allan Elias, with the club also in advanced negotiations to sell Nico González to Newcastle.
body: The 22-year-old Elias – known as Allan – made his senior debut for Palmeiras last year and has made 96 appearances for the club, scoring nine goals and making 12 assists. He is yet to play for Brazil.

Allan’s arrival will clear the way for the sale of his countryman, Savinho, to Tottenham for £75m plus £10m. Spurs also want to sign City’s Omar Marmoush, with the fee for the forward expected to be £75m. While Savinho has informed Enzo Maresca he wishes to leave, City’s manager said on Friday that the Egyptian had not done so.

González is expected to be sold to Newcastle for a fee in the region of £50m, a price almost identical to the £49.8m City paid Porto for the midfielder in the January 2025 window. Newcastle are understood to be confident of signing the 24-year-old.

The money from his proposed sale may be used by City to make an official bid for Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández. While Chelsea set a deadline for any offer for the midfielder of 14 August, which was not met, City may test their resolve, as the player is open to a move and a reunion with his former coach Maresca.

articles.title: Post-Pep Premier League era begins with weekend of hyper-managed shock and awe | Barney Ronay
articles.summary: Possession numbers, the intense physicality and the pure rhythm of games all felt noticeably new as the season began. There has been something oddly narcotic and moreish about the drip-drip of fresh Pep Guardiola content either side of the start of the new Premier League season. Eras come and go.
body: So we have continued to feast on the Pep-at-City visuals: dead jeopardy, reheated beefs, the uplifting team talks of a departed manager to the departed players of a departed team, and moments that often feel far more gripping than the daily churn of what we must, out of habit, call the real world.

The thought occurred watching all this: has the Premier League found its Tupac? Is Pep just going to keep on doing this, dropping new material, fresh hits, posthumous platinum albums? A bald, thin charismatic man who keeps on releasing his lost tapes. We have exactly the thing, sir. Is he even actually dead?

Probably this won’t happen. But a profound absence is still a profound presence at moments like these. The ghosts continue to pull the strings. This weekend was the first of the new Premier League season. More significantly, it was also the first of the post‑Pep era.

articles.title: Villa in talks with Club Brugge for defender Ordonez
articles.summary: Aston Villa are working on a move for Club Brugge central defender Joel Ordonez after failing to agree a deal with Southampton for Taylor Harwood-Bellis.
body: The Premier League side, who sold England defender Ezri Konsa to Arsenal last week, are accelerating their interest in Ordonez, with discussions ongoing and his Belgian Pro League club wanting a minimum £40m fee for the Ecuador international.
The 22-year-old centre-back, who played for his country at this summer's World Cup, has made 124 appearances for Club Brugge since joining in 2022 from Independiente del Valle.
Villa had targeted Harwood-Bellis, but there is understood to be a significant gap in valuation between them and Southampton after an offer worth £18m was rejected.
It remains to be seen whether a transfer for the 24-year-old can still be revived but, as things stand, Unai Emery's side have moved on to other targets.

The RFL chief executive, Nigel Wood, is understood to have circulated the document to the Super League owners last Wednesday, the day before they voted to reject the NRL’s offer.

articles.title: ‘Enough is enough’: players pile pressure on under-fire Gianni Infantino to resign
articles.summary: President accused by ‘Fifa Legends’ of being power hungry. Samuel Eto’o claims chief has not ‘done anything wrong’ A group of influential current and former footballers have added to the pressure on Gianni Infantino by calling for change at the top of Fifa, saying “enough is enough” in a statement…
body: The intervention is particularly significant given some of those behind its circulation have undertaken ambassadorial activities for Fifa as part of its “Fifa Legends” programme. Among them is the former Manchester United and Arsenal defender Mikaël Silvestre, who also sits on the governing body’s 16-member players’ voice panel designed to assist with anti-racism initiatives.

Others to have shared the statement include the England defender Lucy Bronze, the former England keeper David James and the France 1998 World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit. More signatories are expected to follow in a concerted reaction to Infantino’s ill-fated attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup.

“We share the exact same concerns as the millions of fans around the world,” part of the statement read. “Like them, we have watched the game we love drift away from its core values under Fifa’s current leadership. For too long, we’ve seen major decisions taken without players being consulted or considered, and without any regard for the fans who sustain the sport.

articles.title: Uefa chief Ceferin rules out Fifa presidency bid
articles.summary: Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin rules himself out of the running to replace Gianni Infantino, but expects a candidate to challenge the Fifa president's leadership in March.
body: Infantino has faced calls to step down after he scrapped a controversial plan to sell off stakes in Fifa's competitions to private investors following widespread opposition.
Uefa led the backlash to the plan, with its members voting to boycott World Cups unless it was scrapped, while European football's governing body said it has lost confidence in Infantino.
Ceferin, 57, has been widely seen as a potential challenger to Infantino, but says he does not plan to stand for the position at the Fifa Congress in March 2027.

"I'm not interested because of two reasons. One reason is that I love Uefa and I love working here, and I think that at a certain point, it's time to also enjoy life a bit," Ceferin said on the Rest is Politics podcast, external.

articles.title: Healy right to call out 'vile' abuse - McGivern
articles.summary: Linfield chairman Roy McGivern says that manager David Healy was "absolutely right" to call out the "personal" and "vile" abuse directed towards him in recent weeks.
body: Healy told the Belfast Telegraph, external that the abuse he, his players and staff received from Blues supporters in Windsor Park and online in the aftermath of their 3-0 defeat by Ballymena United on the opening day of the Irish Premiership season was "nothing short of disgraceful".
McGivern stressed that while Blues supporters had the right to air their frustrations with performances on the pitch, they should not cross the line when it comes to abusing the manager and players.

"I've met with David this week and had a good chat with him. There are certainly no issues between David and the board. We totally understand fans get frustrated, I've been a fan of this club for well over 50 years and fans who pay their money for the games and season tickets and members tickets, they're entitled to give their opinions and be frustrated," McGivern said.
"That's part and parcel of football, we totally get that and no one is saying that's not acceptable.

articles.title: Super League 'not a carcass to be picked at' - McManus
articles.summary: St Helens chairman Eamonn McManus says the NRL and Super League need to work together - not against each other - to help grow rugby league globally.
body: St Helens chairman Eamonn McManus says the NRL and Super League should be working together to help grow rugby league as a global sport - instead of one organisation taking over from the other.
Super League confirmed earlier in the month that it had received an investment offer from the Australian Rugby League Commission, which plans to help grow the European competition's revenue.
Talks have been ongoing over a deal between the two parties since last year, but McManus said the "whole issue has been gone about in the wrong way".
"It's a case of the NRL, the most successful rugby club competition in the world, looking to acquire or rescue a target that's not functioning," he told BBC Radio Merseyside.

articles.title: Aston Villa Lead Race For £33m Serie A Outcast Striker: Good Option For Emery?
articles.summary: Aston Villa have been linked with a move for Juventus striker Jonathan David, with reports from Ekrem Konur suggesting the Italian club could accept £30.07m-£33.74m for the 26-year-old.
body: There is one problem with the whole argument, though. Villa’s situation has changed dramatically.

Ollie Watkins is no longer the obvious, immovable centre-forward at Villa Park. Al-Hilal are pushing hard for the England international, with Sky Sports reporting that a €45m (£38.5m) offer has already been rejected and negotiations are continuing. That matters a lot.

Morgan Rogers has already left Aston Villa, while Watkins’ future is increasingly uncertain after he missed the opening-day defeat by Brighton amid the Saudi interest. So Villa suddenly do need attacking reinforcements, and that makes the David story rather more interesting.

His first Juventus season was underwhelming: six Serie A goals in 35 appearances, with two more in nine Champions League outings. That is hardly the sort of record you want to see attached to a €40m-plus signing.

articles.title: It's coming, Liverpool make massive bid to sign African star
articles.summary: Liverpool have made a bid to sign an African star. Richard Hughes' time at Liverpool appears to be drawing to a close, with his expected move to Al Hilal bringing an end to a relatively short but eventful spell as sporting director.
body: Assessing his tenure is difficult because it has contained such contrasting periods. Liverpool have enjoyed significant success during his time at the club, but that has been accompanied by several transfer windows in which the recruitment process has appeared increasingly uncertain.

Hughes' first summer was defined by the failure to land Martin Zubimendi, while his third has followed a similar pattern after Yan Diomande opted for Real Madrid. His second window was considerably more productive, with Liverpool securing a number of their primary targets. However, the performances of several of those signings have yet to consistently match the level of investment involved.
That context has inevitably shaped the perception of Hughes as he approaches the end of his tenure.

The role of a sporting director is not simply to identify good players. It is to establish a coherent recruitment strategy, anticipate the needs of the squad and ensure there are credible alternatives when a preferred target becomes unavailable.

articles.title: 'We haven't got the money' - Wolff says Mercedes can't match rivals' upgrade rate
articles.summary: Toto Wolff says Mercedes do not have extra money available to quickly respond to the growing threat from McLaren and Ferrari through car development.
body: The Silver Arrows continue to lead both world championship races, and grew their leads in both standings across the Dutch Grand Prix Sprint weekend, but have seen their early-season dominance eroded in recent months.
After winning the opening six rounds of F1's new rules era, Mercedes have won two races in the last six, the same number as Ferrari and McLaren.

McLaren have taken the last two wins after upgrades to their car at each of the last two events, while Mercedes have brought only smaller revisions to their W17 since its last big update at the Canadian GP in late May.

All teams operate to a yearly budget cap governing car spend, which for 2026 was raised to $215m due to the huge change in regulations, and have to decide how they each allocate spend on car development through the season.

articles.title: Robert Sanchez defies 97% stat with latest gaffe that costs Chelsea
articles.summary: Robert Sanchez has cost Chelsea once again, and is very lucky his team have been good at the other end. If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content.
body: Chelsea are 2-1 up against Fulham after the first half against Fulham at Craven Cottage, but it could have been very different.
The Blues took the lead within 30 seconds with a superb Cole Palmer assist to Joao Pedro, and after that there were a few chances for Xabi Alonso’s team to extend their lead.
But just as they got comfortable, the same old villain returned. Goalkeeper Robert Sanchez looked nervy on the ball, spreading panic though the defence as usual.

Not long after that he was beaten at his near post as Fulham equalised. According to xG, that would have been saved in 97% of instances – not with Rob around. For a while the team were shaken, and the keeper is fortunate that the attack is in good enough shape to score another before the break.

articles.title: Khang, Duncan and Zhang named as Stanford's Solheim Cup captains' picks
articles.summary: Megan Khang, Rose Zhang and Lindy Duncan have been named as Angela Stanford's three captains' picks for next month's Solheim Cup, as Team USA's full 12-player squad was officially confirmed on Monday.
body: Following this weekend's CPKC Women's Open, Andrea Lee and Alison Lee also both earned qualifying spots for Team USA via the Rolex Women's World Golf Rankings.

They will join Nelly Korda, Angel Yin, Jennifer Kupcho, Yealimi Noh, Auston Kim, Lauren Coughlin and Allisen Corpuz, who all qualified automatically for the tournament via the Solheim Cup points list.

Anna Nordqvist confirmed her four captain's picks earlier in August, with both sides now set to face off at Bernardus Golf in The Netherlands on September 11, and all three tournament days will be shown live on Sky Sports Golf.

Duncan, 35, and Kim, 26, are the only two rookies in Stanford's squad for September's tournament. Duncan is also the second-oldest Solheim Cup debutant since Nancy Scranton, who made her first Solheim Cup appearance in 2000, aged 39.

articles.title: When are the Europa and Conference League draws and how do they work?
articles.summary: The Europa League and Conference League league phase draws will see British clubs - including Bournemouth, Sunderland, Crystal Palace - discover their opponents.
body: The Europa League league phase draw - involving Bournemouth, Sunderland and Crystal Palace - takes place at 12pm UK time on Friday. The Conference League draw - which could involve Brighton, Hearts, Hibs, Motherwell, Rangers and Northern Irish team Larne - gets under way straight after.
Twelve teams qualify directly for the league phase of the Europa League, with one slot also reserved for UEFA Conference League title holders, Crystal Palace.

A further 12 sides secure their places by qualifying through the play-off round. The 36-team line-up is completed by 11 losing teams transferring from the UEFA Champions League third qualifying round and play-offs.

Teams who could play Europa League if they lose in the Champions League play-off round: AEK Athens, Bodo/Glimt, Celje, Celtic, Dinamo Zagreb, Fenerbahce, Hapoel Beer-Sheva, LASK, Levski Sofia, Lyon, NEC Breda, Sabah, Slovan Bratislava, Viking Stavanger.
